_about: Every quiz in the course, keyed by lesson id. answer = index 0-3. Built from scripts/modules by build/modules.py.

M00-L1.lesson: What An App Is Made Of

questions.q: What is a table in an app?
options: Where data is stored in rows and columns
A kind of screen for staff
questions.why: A table stores the app's data, with one row per thing and one column per fact.

questions.q: In this course, what is a leak?
options: Someone seeing data that is not theirs
A spelling mistake on a page
questions.why: A leak happens when a wall fails and a person sees data that belongs to someone else.

questions.q: What is kit K00?
options: The floor that every app gets
A kit only for big apps
The last kit to be added
questions.why: K00 is the floor: the basics, the walls between businesses and the legal parts, on every app.

questions.q: Why is building every app by hand a problem when you want many apps?
options: Lessons from one app are not carried to the next
questions.why: Each hand-made app starts from a blank page, so the same mistakes and missed checks repeat.

questions.q: How many stages are on the factory road?
questions.why: The road has nine stages, from 0 Idea to 8 Operate.

questions.q: Which is the only stage that spends build credits?
questions.why: Stage 6 is where the app is built, and it is the only stage that spends build credits.

questions.q: Which of these gates opens by itself when every check passes?
questions.why: Schema is an automatic gate, like Base; Lock and Launch always need a person.

questions.q: What does the Slot check inside Invest make sure of?
options: No more than 3 builds at once, with 1 lane kept for rescues
questions.why: Slot limits building to 3 apps at once and keeps 1 lane free for rescues.

questions.q: What three things does the brief on the Idea Form ask for?
options: What it is, who pays and the pain
questions.why: The one-line brief covers the vision, who pays and the pain.

questions.q: Which of the four idea doors is not built yet?
questions.why: The client door, for ideas from outside customers, is not built yet.

questions.q: What is a reseller?
options: A business that sells the app to its members under its own name
A person who tests the app
questions.why: A reseller, like Northvale Canine Society, sells the app to its own members with its own name on it.

questions.q: What happens when a card needs to change?
options: A new version, such as v2, is saved beside it
The idea starts again with a new name
questions.why: The card is never overwritten, so changes are saved as new versions and the history is kept.

questions.q: How many groups are the 20 codes sorted into?
questions.why: The codes sit in 4 groups: Businesses, Who Signs In, Customers and Public.

questions.q: Which six codes must always be answered?
options: TEN, CUST, SEN, VIEW, POST and PAY
ROLE, JOIN, HELP, GUEST, BELONG and SHARE
PRICE, BRAND, SEND, EXIT, POOL and MEET
questions.why: The factory cannot judge an idea without TEN, CUST, SEN, VIEW, POST and PAY.

questions.q: What does SEN 3 mean?
questions.why: SEN (0-3) runs from ordinary to children, so 3 means the app holds children's data.

questions.q: What does a question mark mean as an answer to one of the 14 optional codes?
questions.why: A question mark honestly records that the answer is not yet known.

M01-L3.lesson: Kill Check, Verdict And Data Role

questions.q: Which kill question asks whether people would use the app once and stop?
questions.why: ONESHOT asks whether people would use it once and stop.

questions.q: No kill answer is yes, but SEN is 3. Which verdict does the engine suggest?
questions.why: SEN 2 or 3 means HOLD until a DPIA is done and signed.

questions.q: What does a PROCESSOR do?
options: Decides why personal data is used
Sells the app under its own name
Handles personal data on behalf of another business
questions.why: A processor follows another business's instructions when it handles personal data.

questions.q: Which idea can never pass the Screen gate automatically?
options: An idea where a kill is suggested
An idea from the Idea Form with no flags
An idea with a short name
questions.why: Kill-suggested, seen-before, AI and client ideas always wait for a person at Screen.

questions.q: Which reviews does the competitor sweep look at most closely?
questions.why: Low-star reviews show what breaks and what annoys people, which is where the gaps are.

questions.q: How many exact customer phrases are collected for the pain?
questions.why: The sweep collects 10 phrases for the pain and 10 for the result, word for word.

questions.q: What does the gap matrix end with?
questions.why: The matrix ends with the 3 strongest gaps, which become the app's edge.

questions.q: Who completes the rules flag?
options: An AI tool on its own
A person, because judging the law needs a human
questions.why: The regulatory flag is a person's line, because no tool can judge the law.

questions.q: What question does the Merit gate ask?
questions.why: Merit asks whether the idea is worth building, after the research is done.

questions.q: At Merit you can name exactly what must change. Which verdict fits?
questions.why: If you can name what to change, the verdict is RESHAPE and the idea goes back to Reception.

questions.q: Why does RECYCLE never apply at Merit?
options: No parts have been built yet
The card is deleted at Merit
questions.why: RECYCLE returns parts to the shelves, and at Merit no parts exist yet.

questions.q: What does the rule "a move writes, or it did not happen" mean?
options: The verdict must be written to the card and register in the same session
The idea must be written twice
Only written ideas can enter Reception
questions.why: A verdict only counts once it is written into the card and the app register in the same session.

questions.q: What does it mean to remix at Stage 2?
options: Start fresh with a blank project
Start from an existing base the factory owns
questions.why: To remix is to start from a base app the factory already owns and change it.

questions.q: What must come with a decision to rebuild as BESPOKE?
options: A dedup check that proved nothing suitable exists
A signed letter from the club
questions.why: A fresh start is only recorded with the dedup run that proved no base fits.

questions.q: Who moves the app through the Base gate?
options: The engine, automatically, when every line is done
questions.why: Base is an auto gate: when every Stage 2 line is done, the engine moves the app on.

questions.q: Why is an Export ZIP taken as soon as the base is chosen?
options: To keep a safe copy to go back to
questions.why: The Export ZIP is a full packed copy, so there is always a safe point to return to.

questions.q: How many bricks are in BRICK-REGISTRY v0.16?
questions.why: The registry in use, v0.16, holds 101 bricks.

questions.q: What is K00?
options: The floor, forced onto every app
questions.why: K00 is the floor: it cannot be picked or removed and sits under every app.

questions.q: Which three bricks make up K00?
questions.why: The floor is BR-BASICS, BR-TENANCY and BR-LEGAL, counted inside every kit.

questions.q: Why does the Body shelf hold the most bricks?
options: Body is the only free shelf
The registry files bot bricks under Body
questions.why: The registry folds Bots into Body, so bot bricks are counted there.

questions.q: What is the launch-minimum scope?
options: Every feature a customer could ever want
The fewest tables and screens that let a first customer pay and use it
questions.why: Launch-minimum is the smallest version a first customer would pay for and use; the rest is roadmap.

questions.q: Why are words, labels and colours stored as data?
options: So a brand swap is an edit to rows, not a paid build turn
So customers can change the code
questions.why: Rows can be changed per brand without paying for a new building turn.

questions.q: Where should a who-sees-and-does-what check happen?
options: On the server side, where the data is held
questions.why: A rule on the server cannot be dodged the way a screen-only rule can.

questions.q: What must the first build include, by the checklist rule?
options: The top three complaints fixed and one thing no rival has
questions.why: The feature lock keeps the three most-counted complaints fixed plus one thing no rival has.

questions.q: What is OBLIGATIONS.csv?
options: A shared file of duties keyed to what causes them
questions.why: It is the shared file of duties, each caused by the platform, a code, a brick or a provider.

questions.q: What happens when a ledger row due at a gate is still open?
options: The gate passes with a warning
questions.why: CK50 stops a gate while any row due at it is open or only part done.

questions.q: Which two conditions does the Lock gate need?
options: A sales page and a domain
A paid prompt and a refund
A named payer and a legal check
questions.why: Lock needs a named payer and a legal check for the scope.

questions.q: What happens to the out list after Lock?
options: Its items join automatically next week
It is closed, and items return only through a new gate
questions.why: The out list closes at Lock; nothing returns by drift.

M05-L1.lesson: How The System Makes The Tables

questions.q: What is a schema?
options: The plan of the tables that hold the data
questions.why: A schema is the plan of the tables, their columns and who may read or write them.

questions.q: Why is the access mode set when a table is created?
options: Because the customer asks for it
Because only resellers can change it
Because setting it then is free and changing it later is a billed turn
questions.why: Setting the mode at creation is free; changing it afterwards costs a builder turn.

questions.q: What does an anonymous probe do?
options: Sends a test request with nobody signed in
questions.why: It checks a table the way a signed-out stranger would reach it.

questions.q: What is the safe way to change a column name?
options: Add a new column, migrate the data, leave the old one unread
Ask customers to type the data again
questions.why: A rename destroys every row, so the factory adds, migrates and leaves the old column unread.

questions.q: Which wall keeps one business's data away from another business?
questions.why: W1, the brand wall, sits between businesses.

questions.q: What should an anonymous read of a control table return?
questions.why: 401 means the signed-out request was refused, which is the pass.

questions.q: Why is a row-level test not enough on a shared table?
options: A shared row has no tenant id, so the test can pass while fields leak
questions.why: On a shared table the leak test must be field-level, because a row-level test passes while leaking.

questions.q: Who moves the app through the Schema gate?
options: The engine, automatically, when every line is done
questions.why: Schema is an auto gate: tables probed and names re-read, then the engine moves the app on.

questions.q: Why does Stage 5 need at least two test tenants?
options: Two tenants make the app load faster
One tenant cannot prove that data stays behind its wall
The build platform charges less for two tenants
The sales page needs two brand names
questions.why: With only one brand there is nobody for data to leak to, so every test passes and proves nothing.

questions.q: What makes the two test tenants contrasting?
options: They use the same colours so tests are fair
They use the same dog names
questions.why: The duty list asks for different names, lanes and colours so that a leak is visible at a glance.

questions.q: How do test members sign in?
options: With an email and password or a magic link, each with their own mailbox
With single sign-on through any account
questions.why: Test members have their own mailboxes and never use Google single sign-on, which signed in the wrong account in real tests.

questions.q: Who sets up the test identities?
options: An AI agent, during the build
Any test member who needs one
The factory owner, once per app, by hand
questions.why: Agents never create accounts; the factory owner sets them up once per app and keeps the logins in a password manager.

questions.q: What is a negative case?
options: A test of the sales page wording
A test that checks something forbidden really fails
A test that is only run on a phone
questions.why: A negative case proves that something which must never happen, such as Brand B reading Brand A's rows, really does fail.

questions.q: Which four kinds of visitor does the test matrix cover?
options: Signed out, Brand A member, Brand B member and owner
questions.why: Every table is checked for a signed-out visitor, a member of each test brand and the owner.

questions.q: What happens when a leak is found during the build?
options: It is noted for a later version
The leak status stays as not tested
questions.why: The gate rules say leaks are watched throughout the build and any leak stops the build.

questions.q: When does the Invest gate pass by itself?
options: When the estimate is 1,500 credits or less and the month's stop line is not passed
Whenever the test plan is written
questions.why: Invest auto-passes at 1,500 credits or less within the month's stop line; above that, the factory owner decides.

questions.q: Why is Stage 6 different from every other stage?
options: It is the only stage with a gate
It is the only stage that uses tables
It is the only stage run by the customer
It is the only stage that spends credits
questions.why: Stage 6 is the only paid stage; every turn of the AI builder spends credits.

questions.q: What does the rule 'an and means two prompts' mean?
options: A request with two jobs is split into two prompts
Every prompt must be sent twice
Two people must write each prompt
Each prompt must name two brands
questions.why: One goal, one surface: if a request needs the word and, it becomes two separate prompts.

questions.q: What does fail closed mean in the walls block?
options: The app shuts down at night
When in doubt, the app refuses access
The builder closes every file it opens
questions.why: Failing closed means the safe answer, no access, is the default whenever the app is unsure.

questions.q: Who runs the tests a prompt carries?
options: The AI builder, inside its own turn
The factory's agents, from outside the app, after the turn
Nobody, the builder's screen is enough
questions.why: Acceptance tests are run from outside; the builder never builds test panels or checks itself inside its turn.

questions.q: What is the first step after every paid turn?
options: Record the prompt and reply word for word
Tell the customer it is ready
questions.why: Record on landing comes before any check, test or reply, so nothing is lost.

questions.q: A file the prompt named did not change after the turn. What does the rule say?
options: Send the same prompt again at once
Ignore it if the screen looks fine
Change the file by hand and move on
The turn failed, so raise a refund ticket and do not resend blind
questions.why: A named file with no change means the turn failed; the factory raises a refund ticket instead of re-prompting blind.

questions.q: Why does the factory check the live code before testing?
options: A cache can still be showing the old version
Live code is cheaper to test
Testing before publishing is not allowed by law
questions.why: A cache keeps saved copies, so tests must confirm the new code is really being served first.

questions.q: What does the Send gate need before the app moves to Launch?
options: A full month of real users
Proved live, with two fresh sign-ins
questions.why: The Send gate rule is proved live, two fresh sign-ins, and the factory owner decides.

questions.q: What does DNS do?
options: It points a domain name at the server where the app lives
It tests every table for leaks
questions.why: DNS is the internet's address book: its records point a name people can type at the server that holds the app.

questions.q: What does a landing page button carry inside its link?
questions.why: The link carries brand and plan; the server then checks the plan is one of that brand's offers.

questions.q: Why is the price never taken from the web address?
options: Anyone can edit a web address
questions.why: A visitor could change the address, so the server looks up the real price from the brand's own offers.

questions.q: Which brands may offer a free plan?
options: The factory owner's own brands, never a reseller's
questions.why: Free is set per brand offer; the owner's brands may offer it, but a reseller brand is never on a free plan.

questions.q: Why does the launch walk include a phone?
options: Phones are faster to test on
The sales page is only shown on phones
Email links opened on a phone can break a journey that works on desktop
questions.why: The walk covers desktop and phone, including email links opened on the phone, because journeys can break between devices.

questions.q: What does the user-switch test check?
options: That two users can share one account
That user B sees none of user A's name or settings in the same browser
That users can switch brands freely
That the owner can sign in as anyone
questions.why: Signing in as A, then out, then in as B in one browser shows whether anything of A's is left behind.

questions.q: Why is checkout tested on the live link?
options: The live link is free to use
The test code only works on phones
questions.why: Checkout does not work in preview, so the 100 percent off test code is used on the live link.

questions.q: What is the status of the weekly boost?
options: A gate the owner must pass
A rule that runs every day
questions.why: The weekly boost line is marked PROPOSED, so it is taught as an idea, not a rule.

questions.q: At what time does the daily leak probe run?
questions.why: The leak probe runs every morning at 06:40 UK time, after the stale check at 06:10.

questions.q: What does the weekly security check cover for each live app?
options: Live links, sign-in and the leak probe
questions.why: A live app joins the weekly security check for its links, its sign-in and its leak probe.

questions.q: When the probe asks a private table for data while signed out, what is the right answer?
questions.why: Private data must refuse a signed-out request; anything else is a leak and raises an incident.

questions.q: What does rule R14 ask for after an app ships?
options: New parts go back to the brick registry
questions.why: R14 sends useful new parts back to the bricks so the next app can reuse them.

questions.q: What does the monthly money line record?
questions.why: The money line records the pounds that came in and went out that month, on the app's card.

questions.q: What happens after two losing months running?
options: The app is deleted at once
A person is asked the Retire question
questions.why: The engine asks a person whether to switch the app off and archive it; asking is not deciding.

questions.q: What does the Return rule R02 say?
options: No new Invest until the app earns back its credits, or 90 days of use show it will
Every app must make money in its first week
Apps return to stage 0 each year
questions.why: Return guards the next spend: no new Invest until the credits are earned back or 90 days show they will be.

questions.q: Who writes the monthly money line?
options: A visitor to the sales page
A person, as named work on the checklist
questions.why: The money line is tagged as the owner's own work, so a person writes it and scripts read it.

questions.q: What moves a live app into Rescue?
options: An open incident tagged to the app
questions.why: The Trouble gate is automatic: an open incident on a stage 8 app moves it to Rescue at the next refresh.

questions.q: Why can a rescue fix move quickly?
options: One build lane is always kept empty for rescue
questions.why: Slot keeps 1 of its 3 lanes for rescue, so the fix never queues; the approvals and tests still happen.

questions.q: Where do a retired app's bricks, kits and proved formations go?
questions.why: Recycle sends the parts of a retired app back to the Reserve room to be used again.

questions.q: What does Re-imagine do?
options: Deletes the app and its row
Points the same assembly at a new audience under a new id
Moves the app back to stage 0
questions.why: Re-imagine keeps the assembly, gives it a new id and audience, and the paid clone goes through Invest.

M10-L1.lesson: Filling In Your First Idea Form

questions.q: Which three answers make up the brief?
options: What it is, who pays, and the pain
questions.why: The brief is what it is, who pays, and the pain it removes, said in plain words.

questions.q: Litterline is TEN 3. What does level 3 mean?
questions.why: TEN (0-6) level 3 means one reseller above the businesses, like a club above its breeders.

questions.q: How many of the 20 codes are required?
questions.why: TEN, CUST, SEN, VIEW, POST and PAY are required; the other 14 may say not yet known.

questions.q: Litterline has no kill answers and SEN 1. Which verdict does the engine suggest?
questions.why: No kill answer and SEN below 2 gives PASS; SEN 2-3 would give HOLD.

questions.q: What must every figure about the future carry in this course?
questions.why: Future figures, such as about 1,000 apps or one a day, are always marked Vision 2029, illustrative.

questions.q: In the Vision 2029 picture, who decides at the human gates?
questions.why: Automation checks and carries between gates, but a person still decides at the human gates.

questions.q: Which plan can a reseller brand be on?
options: Any plan typed into the web address
questions.why: A reseller brand is never on a free plan, and the price is never taken from the web address.

questions.q: What does the course promise about income?
options: Nothing; results depend on your own work
questions.why: There are no income promises; results depend on your own work.
